questions.q: Which report formats can hold a summary formula?
options: Tabular reports only
Summary and matrix reports, which have grouped data
Joined reports only
Every format, including tabular, with no restriction
questions.explain: A summary formula calculates on summarized (grouped) values, so it needs a summary or matrix report. Plain tabular reports do not offer it.

questions.q: Where do you start adding a summary formula in the Lightning Report Builder?
options: The Filters panel
The Chart properties dialog
The report's Subscribe menu
The dropdown next to Columns in the Outline panel
questions.explain: The Columns dropdown offers Add Bucket Column and Add Summary Formula.

questions.q: What does the built-in RowCount represent in a summary formula?
options: The number of records in the group being calculated
The number of columns in the report
The number of groupings in the report
The maximum rows the report may display
questions.explain: RowCount is the number of records in the group (or the grand total), which makes it the denominator for averages and rates.

questions.q: One rep won 1 of 2 deals (50%) and another won 9 of 10 (90%). Why does a summary formula give a better team win rate than averaging the two percentages?
options: Summary formulas ignore the smaller rep's deals
It divides summed values (10 of 12, about 83%), producing a correctly weighted rate
Averages are not allowed in reports
It rounds every rate to 100%
questions.explain: A ratio of sums weights each rep by volume. Averaging 50 and 90 gives 70%, which misstates the true team rate.

questions.q: Why wrap a rate formula in an IF that checks RowCount?
options: To make the column sortable
To change the format to Percent
To avoid errors from dividing by zero in empty groups
To allow the formula on tabular reports
questions.explain: A group with no records would divide by zero. Guarding with IF on RowCount keeps the report clean.
